=== DOCS-TRUTH SUMMARY (verified 2026-06-08 against trino.io/docs/467) ===
• two-level-macro-median: Trino has NO `MEDIAN` function (verbatim r23:1246 + r23:141-159 + r05:2261 inoculations). Use `approx_percentile(x, 0.5)` for BOTH the inner per-group median AND the outer aggregate (or `AVG` of per-group medians for the outer). The two-level shape is CTE-then-outer-aggregate (per r07:999 'aggregate inside its own scalar subquery / CTE'). Column-scope discipline (per r23:1249): the inner CTE MUST project the per-group aggregate under an explicit alias; the outer query references the alias, not a conceptual expression.
• MAX(COUNT(*)) directly: nested-aggregate parse error in Trino (same restriction as Postgres/Snowflake; aggregate of aggregate not allowed). Required rewrite: (a) inner CTE with COUNT(*) GROUP BY user, weekday → outer MAX per user, OR (b) ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user ORDER BY weekday_count DESC) AS rn → outer WHERE rn = 1 (preferred when you ALSO need the weekday label).
• multi-key dim-JOIN: ANSI-SQL ON clause accepts conjunctions: ON a.k1=b.k1 AND a.k2=b.k2 is the standard composite-key JOIN form. Documented worked examples at r09:296 (users_dim is_current = TRUE) and r13:3297 (Postgres-region composite key MERGE). r08 star-schema primitive (single-key dim-JOIN) generalizes mechanically.
• two-threshold HAVING: HAVING COUNT(*) > 50 AND SUM(amount) > 10000 valid in ONE clause (verified verbatim at trino.io/docs/467/sql/select.html on prior iter663 — HAVING controls which groups are selected via aggregate expressions; boolean conjunction of aggregate expressions is the standard form, no need to split into a CTE chain or layered HAVING).
